title: Charles Buhler leaves NASA to found Exodus Space

tellings.quote: Leaving NASA and starting his own company, Exodus Space, based on propellantless propulsion, which he attributes to Thomas Towns and Brown.
But there's the lead electrostatic scientist from NASA at Cape Kennedy just left to start a private propellantless propulsion company
tellings.difference: Calls him NASA's lead electrostatics scientist at Cape Kennedy, and does not name the company.
tellings.link_reason: Both tell of Charles Buhler leaving NASA to start a propellantless propulsion company that he credits to Townsend Brown.

as_told.title: NASA electrostatics lead Charles Buhler leaves to start a propellantless propulsion company
as_told.place_text: NASA Kennedy Space Center, Cape Kennedy

plain: A scientist named Charles Buhler, whom Michels calls NASA's lead electrostatics scientist at Cape Kennedy, is said to have left NASA to start his own company, Exodus Space, built on propellantless propulsion, meaning moving a craft without burning or throwing out fuel. Michels tells it on two episodes and says Buhler credits the idea to Thomas Townsend Brown, an earlier researcher of high-voltage propulsion, as a sign such work has moved from fringe to industry.
